messages.subject: Re: Newbie question: what files in packrat do I check in to git
messages.subject_clean: Newbie question: what files in packrat do I check in to git
messages.body_plain:
At minimum, you need to check in the packrat/packrat.lock file — Packrat should know how to restore based on that, unless you are using packages within local repositories not available on other system. You should also check in the project .Rprofile as well as packrat/init.R, to ensure that we automatically enter packrat mode upon starting an R session in that directory. Finally, you should also check in the packrat/packrat.opts file, although this is not strictly necessary.

When calling packrat::restore() from an empty project with just a lockfile, Packrat will automatically find, download, and install packages as needed (presuming it can locate them)

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.subject: Re: Packrat and Source Control
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

Sorry -- the collaboration section needs to be updated. But, in short, at minimum you need to upload the `packrat/packrat.lock` file, but it's recommended that you also upload the project `.Rprofile`, `packrat/packrat.opts` and `packrat/init.R`. You may want to upload the package sources as well (to ensure that dependencies are available in case you, for example, did not have internet access) but that is more personal preference.

As long as the `packrat.lock` file is available, you should be able to call `packrat::restore()` to restore the project library (and this is what collaborators should do -- clone the project, `packrat::restore()`, and then go ahead and work.)

messages.subject: Re: Can packrat projects using different R versions run concurrently on Shiny Server
messages.subject_clean: Can packrat projects using different R versions run concurrently on Shiny Server
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

We currently have one fairly complex app that is using 3.0.2 and is not set up in packrat. This runs on open source Shiny Server. We want to add a new packrat project to the server, built on 3.1.1, but obviously want to avoid any conflicts. Our first app ran into problems running on 3.1.1, I believe the issue is related to dplyr changes which occurred between those versions of R. Based on your comments, testing the new app on 3.0.2 might be the best approach. BTW, we are in the process of purchasing Shiny Server Pro but until that is in place we need a work around. Thanks for the r_path info.

James
